verdict.summary: Any owner, admin or manager on a Klaviyo account can create an OAuth app and connect it right away. Customers can install it from a shared install URL with no review, but they see an 'app not reviewed' warning. Review only applies to removing that warning and getting listed in the App Marketplace. Listing is much harder: you need partner status, 5 live customer installs, security and registration forms, and a detailed testing doc. Composio has no managed app for Klaviyo, so you must register your own.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min to connect your own account and share the install URL; several days to prepare a marketplace submission
verdict.approval_wait: None for installs from a shared URL (customers see a warning). Marketplace review time is not published.

gates.name: Your own Klaviyo account (unreviewed app)
gates.unlocks: Create the OAuth app in Manage apps and connect your own Klaviyo account through Composio.
limits: Only owner, admin or manager roles can create apps and grant consent
Access tokens last about 1 hour per the 2026 docs (10 min in the 2023 docs); go by expires_in
Refresh tokens are revoked after 90 days without use
Older docs describe an allowlist gate: a 404 on klaviyo.com/oauth/client means your company is not enabled

gates.name: Customer installs from a shared installation URL (unlisted, unreviewed)
gates.unlocks: Any Klaviyo account (owner/admin/manager) can install your app from the installation URL you share. The app does not need to be listed.

No user or install cap is documented
Tokens belong to the Klaviyo account, not the individual user
The app must support installs from klaviyo.com and any of its subdomains

gates.name: Reviewed app / App Marketplace listing
gates.unlocks: Removes the unreviewed-app warning and gets your app listed in Klaviyo's App Marketplace / integration directory.
limits: Requires Klaviyo tech partner status, and not everyone is eligible
At least 5 active customer installs with production API traffic; your own or company accounts don't count
Registration and security forms are required, one security form per app
Klaviyo may decline to list an app for any reason
High error rates can get an app delisted
gates.time_to_reach: Weeks or more: you need 5 live customer installs, partner approval and a review whose length is not published

steps.title: Confirm your Klaviyo role and access
steps.detail: Log in to Klaviyo as an owner, admin or manager. Only these roles can create OAuth apps or approve an install. If klaviyo.com/oauth/client returns a 404, older docs say your company has not been enabled for OAuth and you should contact your Klaviyo account contact.
gotchas: The allowlist gate comes from the 2023 docs. The 2026 docs don't mention it, so it may no longer apply.

steps.title: Create the app in Manage apps
steps.detail: Go to Integrations > Developers > Manage apps and click Create app. Give it a name, then copy the client ID and client secret right away.
gotchas: The client secret is shown only once. If you lose it, generate a new one.

steps.title: Choose the smallest scope set you need
steps.detail: List the Klaviyo endpoints your agent actually calls and map each one to a scope. Enter the scopes on the app as a space-separated list. accounts:read is always included. Composio's default list includes many write scopes; remove any you don't use.
gotchas: Klaviyo rejects apps in review that request more scopes than they use. Example from the docs: a reporting app should not request campaigns:write, flows:write, tags or templates.

steps.title: Add the Composio redirect URI to the allowlist
steps.detail: In the app's redirect URI allowlist, paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config. The redirect_uri in each authorization request must match an allowlisted entry exactly. Separate multiple entries with spaces or newlines.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Trailing slashes and http vs https must match exactly.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config with your credentials
steps.detail: In Composio, create an auth config for the klaviyo toolkit using OAuth2 with your own client ID and secret, plus the trimmed scope list. Klaviyo's authorize endpoint is https://www.klaviyo.com/oauth/authorize. Its token endpoint is https://a.klaviyo.com/oauth/token (server-side form POST with HTTP Basic client credentials). Klaviyo requires PKCE with S256.
gotchas: Since March 31, 2025, Klaviyo blocks token and revoke calls sent through www.klaviyo.com. Use a.klaviyo.com.
Composio has no managed Klaviyo app, so your own credentials are required.

steps.title: Connect your own Klaviyo account
steps.detail: Start a Composio connection, log in as an owner/admin/manager and approve the install. Then make a test API call, such as reading accounts, to confirm the token works.
gotchas: Authorization codes expire after 5 minutes, so the callback must exchange them right away.
Tokens apply to the whole Klaviyo account, not just the user who approved.

steps.title: Share the installation URL with customers
steps.detail: Give customers an installation URL that requires them to be logged in and then goes straight into the OAuth flow. No listing is needed. Customers will see a warning that Klaviyo has not reviewed the app, but they can still install and use it.
gotchas: Install must work from klaviyo.com and from any of its subdomains.
Handle install, uninstall and error paths; high error rates can lead to delisting later.
A refresh token unused for 90 days is revoked, so refresh tokens regularly or plan for reconnects.

steps.title: Get 5 active customer installs
steps.detail: Before you can submit for review, at least 5 customer accounts must have the app installed and be making production API calls. Developer accounts, test accounts and accounts linked to your company don't count.

steps.title: Apply for partner status and complete the registration and security forms
steps.detail: Fill out Klaviyo's tech partner application. Submit the app registration form, which binds your company to the Technology Partner Agreement, the Acceptable Use Policy and the API Terms of Use. Complete one security form for each app.
gotchas: Not every applicant is eligible for partner status.
Submitting without these forms leads to rejection.
Security requirements: TLS 1.2+, OAuth tokens encrypted at rest (e.g. AES-256), credentials kept in a secrets manager and rotated, and logs retained for 365 days.

steps.title: Prepare the testing doc and listing assets
steps.detail: Copy Klaviyo's testing template into a Google Doc and give it commenter access. Cover the install workflow, each endpoint and its scopes, an architecture diagram, a recorded demo and OAuth test details. Draft the listing: developer name (30 characters max), short description (75 max), full description (300 max), primary category, a 48x48 SVG logo with no scripts, 4-8 gallery images or one cover image, 2-6 key features, a user guide, and installation, settings, pricing, support, website and privacy policy URLs.
gotchas: Links to public documentation are not accepted in place of the testing doc.
You record the demo video yourself.

steps.title: Give reviewers test access without sharing credentials
steps.detail: Add Klaviyo's review email address to your test account, or send a password reset to that address. Never put credentials in the submission or in an email.

steps.title: Submit for review
steps.detail: Go to Integrations > Developers > Manage apps, click your app and choose Review submission. Confirm the Authentication, Company details (company name, description, website, review contact email), App listing, and Registration & security sections, then submit.

steps.title: Wait for Klaviyo's technical and security review
steps.detail: Klaviyo reviews the app for technical quality and security. If it's rejected, you get detailed reasons and can resubmit after making changes. Klaviyo does not publish a review timeline and may decline to list an app for any reason.

requirements.item: Owner, admin or manager role on a Klaviyo account
requirements.detail: Needed to create the app and to approve installs.
Klaviyo requires PKCE. The code verifier must be 43-128 characters.
Token exchange and refresh go to https://a.klaviyo.com/oauth/token. Calls through www.klaviyo.com are blocked.

requirements.item: Exact match on the redirect URI
requirements.detail: The redirect_uri must exactly match an entry on the app's allowlist.

requirements.item: Installs from klaviyo.com and its subdomains
requirements.detail: The OAuth app must handle installs started from any klaviyo.com subdomain.
Must show production API traffic. Your own and company accounts don't count.

requirements.item: Klaviyo tech partner status and registration form
requirements.detail: Required for a directory listing. The form binds you to the TPA, AUP and API Terms.
One security form per app. TLS 1.2+, tokens encrypted at rest, secrets manager with rotation, 365-day log retention.

requirements.item: Testing doc as a Google Doc with commenter access
requirements.detail: Based on Klaviyo's template, with architecture diagram, demo video, endpoints/scopes and OAuth test details.
Text with character limits, SVG logo, gallery, key features, user guide, plus installation, settings, pricing, support, website and privacy policy URLs.
Over-scoped apps are rejected in review.

scopes.effect: Included by default and can't be removed.
Klaviyo has no scope tiers, but review rejects write scopes your app doesn't use. Composio's default list includes many of them, so trim it before submitting.
Request these only if you actually call those endpoints. The review guide gives them as examples of unnecessary scopes for a reporting app.

blockers.cause: Per the 2023 docs, your company hasn't been allowlisted for the OAuth feature.
blockers.fix: Contact your Klaviyo account contact to request access. This gate may no longer apply.

blockers.symptom: Can't create an app or approve an install
blockers.cause: Your Klaviyo user is not an owner, admin or manager.
blockers.fix: Use an account with one of those roles, or ask an owner to upgrade your role.

blockers.cause: The Composio callback is not on the allowlist exactly as sent.
blockers.fix: Paste the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config into the app's redirect allowlist.

blockers.symptom: Token exchange or refresh fails or is blocked
blockers.cause: Requests are going through www.klaviyo.com, or the 5-minute code expired.
blockers.fix: Use https://a.klaviyo.com/oauth/token and exchange codes right away.

blockers.symptom: Connection stops working after a long idle period
blockers.cause: Refresh tokens unused for 90 days are revoked.
blockers.fix: Refresh tokens regularly, or have the user reconnect.

blockers.cause: The app requests scopes it doesn't use, e.g. Composio's broad default list.
blockers.fix: Cut scopes down to only the endpoints you call, then resubmit.

blockers.symptom: Submission rejected, or you can't submit at all
blockers.cause: Missing registration or security forms, or fewer than 5 qualifying customer installs.
blockers.fix: Complete both forms for each app and reach 5 active customer installs with production traffic.

blockers.symptom: App not listed even after passing review
blockers.cause: Klaviyo may decline to list an app for any reason.
blockers.fix: Keep distributing through your installation URL, which works without a listing.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Klaviyo, so you must register your own and enter its client ID and secret in a Composio auth config. Add the callback URL shown in that auth config to the Klaviyo app's redirect allowlist exactly. Composio's default scope list includes many write scopes, so trim it to what your agent uses, especially if you plan to submit for Klaviyo review.

open_questions: Does the 2023 'limited availability' allowlist (404 on /oauth/client) still apply? The 2026 docs don't mention it.
Klaviyo does not publish a review turnaround time.
Klaviyo doesn't document whether it accepts Composio's callback URL on the redirect allowlist. Test it.
Access token lifetime differs between doc versions (1 hour vs 10 min). Rely on expires_in.
Composio's handling of PKCE (S256) for Klaviyo was not checked here. Confirm the auth config sends a code_challenge.
Do private (non-marketplace) apps need partner status? The docs only tie partner status to directory listing.
The console UI and consent screen sit behind a login and could not be inspected, so field labels may differ slightly.
A third-party source says OAuth tokens have their own rate limits separate from API keys. Klaviyo's docs were not checked on this.
